Measurement honesty: 'worst event-loop stall' is a loop-lag watcher task (asyncio.sleep(0.001), excess over 1 ms, max over the awaited call) - it measures loop latency including GIL-holding worker threads (hence the residual ~250 ms data: stall the evidence admits) and by definition cannot see a GIL-releasing worker; 'off the loop' is proven by `test_no_full_body_digest_runs_on_the_event_loop` (asserts no `digest_of` in store/prepare/fetch sees a running loop in its thread) and its three mutants, not by the harness. tracemalloc high-water is process-wide (all threads, Python allocator only), `reset_peak` + baseline per operation, in a separate pass with nothing else running in the process. Results are under models/marlin2b/results/M4-<label>.jsonl on the branch as the brief's owned path requires, named consistently; code_sha in env rows checked (7582242, 51d3e0d, d99a0bb, 28e54b5, 0d86e2c, 8179144, 0b9f78b). No blocking defect, no MEDIA-SEC/PARITY regression; the four findings are oracle-strength and wording items. All my numbers are meas. on the shared development host at 1-minute load ~40-46 (heavier than the implementer's 13-31), not the pilot box.
